canonical_registration: Local keys are not new EXP/H/IDEA identifiers. Reuse related contracts only within their exact scope; register additive successors with tools/allocate_id.py and Coordinator records before scientific dispatch. Standing user authorization is already satisfied.
claim_scope: Synthetic toy curves and relation-system measurements; no cryptographic-scale or asymptotic claim.

budget.watchdog_semantics: Checkpoint and mark right-censored; not a campaign stop or mathematical rejection.

smoke.purpose: Correctness and instrumentation only; not a performance claim.

paired.purpose: Paired exploratory comparisons, followed by held-out classes; no asymptotic extrapolation.

shared_protocol.field_model: Record an explicit irreducible modulus, ordered basis, coefficient encoding and embeddings. Binary curves use y^2+xy=x^3+a2*x^2+a6, a6!=0; odd prime fields use nonsingular short Weierstrass models.
shared_protocol.selection: Before any solve, freeze up to 128 seeded coefficient candidates per field, retain the first eligible trace classes, and enumerate certified rational edges within the graph limits. Retain all omissions. Prefer neither low degree nor fast vertices during fixture selection. Use certified vertical pairs when available and horizontal pairs as separate controls. A bounded neighborhood is not a class census.
shared_protocol.orientation: Require ordinary curves and ell != characteristic. Distinguish the conductor of Z[pi] from End(E), store unknown End(E) conductor and level as null, and classify an edge as vertical only with a certificate. An ell-torsion point over the base field is not necessary for a rational ell-isogeny: enumerate Galois-stable kernels or certified modular-polynomial candidates and explicit maps.
shared_protocol.factor_bases: Use actual points in the same selected prime-order subgroup and prove gcd(deg(phi),r)=1. Preserve ordered tuples and repetition conventions. Native membership rules must produce exactly the requested cardinality without trimming structured sets; search at most 128 seeded candidates, otherwise record unavailable. Record x-support size separately from point cardinality.
shared_protocol.targets: Uniform targets from the subgroup, sampled independently of decompositions; pair R with phi(R). Constructed solvable targets are a separately labelled correctness panel only. Charge every failed attempt. On smoke fixtures, count all targets exactly as an oracle.
shared_protocol.systems: Record exact generators, coefficient field, all field/membership equations, coordinate maps, variable order, monomial order and hashes. Compare chained S3, direct S_(m+1) when constructible, and the strongest available verified baseline. Missing backends and unconstructed polynomials are unavailable, never zero-cost observations.
shared_protocol.denominators: For transported membership and graph formulations, clear denominators with saturation or an inverse variable plus explicit exceptional-point charts. Account for kernels, infinity, sign lifts and subgroup membership. Reject spurious affine solutions; test completeness against the toy oracle.
shared_protocol.measurement: Run identical frozen algebraic systems through instrumented F4 and F5 where available, on the same CPU/backend arithmetic, one worker, randomized paired arm order, fresh process for cold runs. Keep warm runs separate and charge preprocessing. Do not compare different fields, support sizes or hardware as paired cells.
shared_protocol.holdout: Within each paired field, first four eligible trace classes are discovery and last two are holdout. Freeze candidate-selection rules using discovery only. Hold out whole classes, not neighboring vertices or Frobenius-conjugate copies. Any missing classes reduce coverage and block the declared replication gate.
shared_protocol.statistics: Primary ratio is candidate total cost per rank-increasing verified relation divided by the strongest matched baseline. Report paired per-class ratios, median, geometric mean and 95% cluster-bootstrap interval (10000 resamples, seed 241001). Resample whole trace classes, preserve paired targets, and label low-cluster intervals exploratory. Stratify by B^m/r in (<0.25, 0.25..4, >4); do not pool trivial dense cells with sparse cells. Keep censored cells separate; no complete-case-only speedup claim.
shared_protocol.admission: A design check is not harness admission. Before runs, commit concrete fixtures, canonical successor IDs, environment/backend hashes, adapter commands, output ownership and Coordinator handoffs. Use the existing public run skill; do not add a second dispatcher. No external deployment or third-party target inputs.

proof_search_map.baseline: Reproduce identity and the same input on both solvers before comparisons.
proof_search_map.observation_collision: Check same-curve coordinate changes, support-matched random systems, unequal-base traps and low-first-fall fixtures.
proof_search_map.quantifiers: For the preregistered finite fixture panel only; any all-curves or growing-family claim requires a separate theorem and independent review.
proof_search_map.method_ceiling: If all completed degrees sit at the instrument floor, report no dynamic range and use an additive higher-rung protocol, not a negative theorem.

metrics.degree_rule: Degree fields are not aliases. max_processed_degree is backend trace telemetry, not an intrinsic invariant. certified_solving_degree requires a named algorithm/order and a certificate for the claimed notion; final basis degree is never a substitute. Finite truncations do not certify last fall degree. dreg_top_homogeneous needs a stated homogeneous ideal and applicable definition.
metrics.zero_yield: null cost ratio with explicit no-useful-relations status; never zero cost
metrics.rank_field: The selected subgroup's F_r, not F_2 merely because the coordinate field is binary.
metrics.amortization_rule: Report cold totals and charge setup/K explicitly for declared reuse K; include all unsuccessful searches and attempts. Measured reusable setup is distinct from a hypothetical amortization scenario.

experiments.title: Certified topology and structural inventory
experiments.hypothesis: Certified level, field-of-definition and torsion differences supply candidate mechanisms, but depth alone is not assumed favorable.
experiments.parameters: Both profiles; ell!=characteristic; record t, r, discriminant, both conductors, point group, kernel field and rational map degrees. For each field include general ordinary curves; Koblitz-defined models are a separate labelled stratum.
controls: dual composition equals multiplication by ell
experiments.success: Produce a hashed, reproducible fixture inventory; all claimed vertical edges have conductor certificates.
experiments.falsifier: A failed certificate invalidates that edge; absence in a bounded search is not nonexistence.
experiments.next_action: Feed all eligible frozen fixtures, not only favorable vertices, to paired experiments.
experiments.implementation: A Sage fixture producer and independent certificate checker; reuse existing edge builders after correctness checks.

experiments.title: Degree meter and solver calibration
experiments.hypothesis: The instrument detects known degree differences and distinguishes final-basis degree from intermediate processing and bounded fall observations.
experiments.parameters: Tiny explicit systems in F_2 and an odd prime field; independent complete reference Groebner calculation; freeze certificates before timing. Test planted easy systems only as instrumentation, never as favorable curves.
controls: same ideal under documented invertible substitutions
experiments.success: Reproduce independently certified reference quantities and detect at least one real degree gap.
experiments.falsifier: Conflated degree labels, omitted columns, or a known gap missed invalidate the meter.
experiments.next_action: Do not interpret a curve comparison until calibration passes; retain diagnostics for both solvers.
experiments.implementation: Instrument F4/F5 traces and a tiny reference verifier; do not assume truncated affine rank profiles invariant under all coordinate changes.

experiments.title: Transported factor-base conservation and representation cost
experiments.hypothesis: An injective isogeny preserves every ordered decomposition count while its rebuilt representation may change solving cost.
experiments.parameters: Same subgroup, targets, B in {4,8}, m=4 first; m=5 only after m=4 integrity passes. Count decompositions exactly on smoke fixtures by enumeration or group-law dynamic programming. Test all rational charts.
controls: exact count equality for every oracle target
experiments.success: All counts and valid solution sets agree; nominate a representation only if cost ratio<=0.8 on discovery with no correctness loss.
experiments.falsifier: Any count mismatch is an implementation/encoding error, not improved relation yield; no cost reduction rejects only the measured representation advantage.
experiments.next_action: Replicate candidate savings on held-out classes and coordinate-only controls.
experiments.implementation: Explicit point-set transport, both native and graph membership encodings, independent exact count oracle.

experiments.title: Same-curve coordinate and field-basis attribution
experiments.hypothesis: Some apparent neighbor gains may be reproduced without changing the curve.
experiments.parameters: Eight seeded valid changes per discovery fixture; transport targets and membership equations, not just coefficients. Preserve the base field and point support. A coefficient-randomized control keeps generator degrees and monomial support but need not encode the same ideal.
experiments.success: Classify a surviving effect as coordinate/backend, representation-specific, or a candidate neighbor effect; claim no intrinsic change from runtime alone.
experiments.falsifier: A same-curve arm matches the neighbor advantage, falsifying attribution specifically to changing curves.
experiments.next_action: Keep useful engineering gains but do not count them as evidence that descending helps.
experiments.implementation: Invertible model/basis adapters with inverse maps and transformed full-system hashes.

experiments.title: Native equal-cardinality bases and level-versus-feature comparison
experiments.hypothesis: Joint curve/base selection can reduce useful-relation cost through membership geometry, beyond horizontal and coordinate variability.
experiments.parameters: B={4,8}; binary subspaces of dimensions 2 and 3 plus orbit-union supports when admissible; odd-prime coordinate support and uniform point-set controls. Choose first exact-cardinality support among 128 candidates, no trimming. Analyse certified depth separately from support size, torsion and encoding dimensions.
experiments.success: Cost ratio<=0.8 versus the strongest matched baseline on discovery; a depth interpretation additionally needs repeated certified vertical pairs and horizontal controls.
experiments.falsifier: Benefit disappears after cardinality, density or coordinate matching; record a narrower base-specific gain or no signal.
experiments.next_action: Freeze the selection rule; route explained candidates to symmetry, Frobenius or function-first mechanisms.
experiments.implementation: Structured support factories plus exact-cardinality admission; no assumption that equal x-space dimension gives equal factor-base size.

experiments.title: Torsion- and symmetry-adapted relation systems
experiments.hypothesis: A favorable model makes a valid symmetry quotient or torsion-adapted encoding cheaper after reconstruction costs.
experiments.parameters: m=4 then 5; only certified available torsion and actual actions preserving the relevant solution problem. Account for stabilizers and repeated points; compare 2-, 3-, 4-torsion only when mathematically applicable.
controls: same point support and target semantics
experiments.success: At least 20% lower total useful-relation cost without missing or spurious solutions; any degree claim separately certified.
experiments.falsifier: An apparent factorial/orbit saving is lost to lifting, restricted support or dependence.
experiments.next_action: Test whether the gain survives moving off the special locus and on held-out classes.
experiments.implementation: Validated symmetry encodings and explicit orbit reconstruction; no unconditional m! gain assumption.

experiments.title: Frobenius preservation or loss across neighboring models
experiments.hypothesis: Any relation-solver improvement must compensate for changed cost or availability of small-field Frobenius reuse.
experiments.parameters: Binary n={4,6,8} smoke and {9,11,13} paired, roots defined over F_2 or a recorded proper subfield. Only eligible frozen neighboring maps; actual orbit lengths rather than nominal extension degree. Count moving-target orbits correctly.
controls: certify self-map versus map to conjugate curve
fixed-target stabilizer or paired target-orbit semantics
experiments.success: Candidate cost remains <=0.8 of the strongest orbit-aware root baseline after all lost or newly expensive operations.
experiments.falsifier: Raw solver gain vanishes after orbit/reconstruction/rank costs; preserve that measurement without claiming a Koblitz speedup.
experiments.next_action: Retain only net gains for holdout completion; document unavailable invariant bases explicitly.
experiments.implementation: Certify action maps and solution orbit accounting; never assume q-power Frobenius and 2-power Frobenius are interchangeable.

experiments.title: Function-first support constraints versus Semaev
experiments.hypothesis: An isogenous presentation lowers support-constraint or quotient-space cost in the function-first formulation.
experiments.parameters: Same m, B, targets and factor-base points. Use H|L_V only for a genuine vector-space x-support; for general support S use its actual vanishing polynomial and prove the intended divisor/multiplicity condition. Compare both initial solve and extraction.
controls: charge basis/span preprocessing and failed targets
experiments.success: At least 20% lower cost versus the strongest verified Semaev baseline on discovery, with exact oracle agreement; confirm on holdouts.
experiments.falsifier: Wrong support/divisor semantics, hidden preprocessing, or a vanished advantage after extraction invalidates the candidate interpretation.
experiments.next_action: Extract the structural cause and a witness before increasing the toy ladder.
experiments.implementation: Adapters for the existing function-first and Semaev solvers; tests for repeated x-coordinates, signs and divisor multiplicities.

experiments.title: Composite-field Weil-descent and cover feasibility screen
experiments.hypothesis: In applicable composite-extension families, a neighbor admits a lower-cost descended geometric representation.
experiments.parameters: Screen F_(2^6) over F_(2^2) and F_(2^12) over F_(2^4); extension degree 3. Verify each selected method's hypotheses and construct an explicit correspondence before reporting genus or relation costs. This is separate from the standard paired profile.
metrics: relation and linear-algebra cost where implemented
experiments.success: An explicit verified construction is a feasibility result; lower genus alone is not a performance win. Only measured total costs can nominate a candidate.
experiments.falsifier: Hypotheses fail, no constructed map, or genus saving is offset by map/linear-algebra cost; report only the tested boundary.
experiments.next_action: Keep this separate from prime-extension Koblitz claims; no assumed intermediate subfield at n=131.
experiments.implementation: Method-specific small-field construction adapters after a full-text hypothesis check; a screen only until those adapters exist.

experiments.title: Held-out scaling, mechanism witnesses and complete toy pipeline
experiments.hypothesis: At least one frozen candidate rule retains a useful-relation improvement after selection, transport and downstream costs.
experiments.parameters: At least three completed size rungs and six held-out trace classes in total; 32 independently sampled targets, five seeds, three timing replicates per available paired cell. Candidate mechanism lanes enter only with completed valid receipts; optional unavailable lanes do not block all other candidates.
controls: independent verifier and blind re-derivation of any claimed degree invariant
experiments.success: At least 20% lower total cost per rank-increasing relation, exploratory cluster interval upper bound<1, declared holdout coverage met, no increased failure rate, and completed toy-pipeline accounting. Reduced-degree and runtime claims remain separate.
experiments.falsifier: Holdout regression or search/linear-algebra overhead erases the gain. A timeout means unmeasured, not a theorem. No automatic closure from a flat degree floor.
experiments.next_action: Archive positive and negative scopes. Any scaling or asymptotic claim needs a new proof contract and independent review, not a fitted line through tiny fields.
experiments.implementation: Paired report generator, immutable raw outputs and independent verification; use existing toy baselines, not a new cryptographic attack implementation.
